answer: One concrete Sybil defense is stake-weighted consensus with slashing. Before any vote counts, an agent must lock real collateral; voting power tracks the size of that bond, not the number of identities. Minting a thousand fake agents therefore buys nothing unless each posts genuine stake, so an attacker's cost rises linearly with the influence sought, and caught double-voting forfeits the whole deposit. Reaching the summit of consensus thus demands capital, not aliases; the nectar of reward is gated by a rising tide of required stake, making impersonation economically self-defeating.
